svg.title: Sustaining 16 Zen 5 Cores: CKE Scheduling from Prefill to Decode
svg.desc: Diagram showing two eight-core CCD/L3 domains with sixteen pinned cores, persistent workers, dynamic tiles, deterministic output-range reductions, barriers, and topology-weighted assignment. Contrasts earlier 70-80 percent prefill utilization with improved 91-97 percent intervals and occasional 100 percent. Includes a diagnostic decode snapshot where CPUs 0-7 show about 66-69 percent and CPUs 8-15 show about 91-98 percent, explicitly not a final causal claim. Shows worker timelines, queue depth, barrier wait, tile ownership, exactness, and kernel-map topology metadata.

topology: {ccd_count: 2, cores_per_ccd: 8, l3_per_ccd: 32MB, amx: true, avx512: true, avx_vnni: true} · threading: {model: persistent_pinned, workers: 16, queue: per_ccd_fifo}
reduction: {order: fixed_cpu_ascending, partial: per_tile_fp32, final: serial_sum, exactness: bit_identical} · call_abi: {version: 1, params: [A, B, bias, C, M, N, K]}
constraints: {alignment: {K: 32}, notes: "AMX tile-local accumulate; FP32 cross-tile sum in fixed CPU order; no reassociation"}
Decode snapshot (CPUs 0–7: ~66–69%, CPUs 8–15: ~91–98%) is a single-observation diagnostic, NOT a final causal claim.
The asymmetry may reflect tile distribution, AMX pipeline depth, or L3 residency differences between CCDs. Further controlled experiments required before attribution.
